assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph frames one question rather than a model: how recipient-directed care can matter amid hostile involvement when neither complete intention nor outcome is available. It reads a represented card gesture and a qualified care candidate (the OS-reported gift of his escape resource, the incompletely marked request to help that child) and refuses both a pure-villain and a vindicated-martyr account. Not D: two located acts and one reported act, with intention explicitly withheld.

The local sequence (named confrontation, card gesture, reported gift and request, rescue proposals, another teacher's return) is stated to be a change in what the reader can consider, not a before-and-after biography; processing order is not a dated course. E rather than NOT_ASSESSED because the monograph affirmatively bounds the sequence.

No wording of his is quoted or characterized; E006 warns that some Prenapates tags may contain adjacent speakers, and the monograph declines any audible delivery. Absence is not evidence of a register.
The monograph states that it gives no supported hobby, meal, sensory taste or domestic routine, and that other characters' company cannot be lent to him. This is a gap, not a trait.

Three local relations with different access: Shiroko (the abduction allegation kept with her; the most plausible recipient of the reported gift), current Sensei (counterpart recognition without shared interiority or interchangeable motives), and the OS whose interpretation of trust belongs to her own developing understanding. Not D: no conduct is shown toward any counterpart beyond the confrontation.

One inward line, the request to help that child, whose speaker and recipient are only contextually marked; the monograph allows a qualified Prenapates reading and refuses an unqualified private confession.

The card display is a represented gesture in the confrontation; threat ownership is uncertain because tags may contain adjacent speakers, and no victor, expenditure or sequence is printed. Not D: one encounter with only one securely attributed act.
The possible gift and request are read as recipient-directed care, not as deliberation; no weighing of alternatives is analyzed.

One 20-paragraph monograph synthesized from maintained Final-volume checkpoints (C003, C004), the E006-E008 episode readings and the working account, which it says add no primary, native or performed-voice reading. None of those inputs is curated on this subject. Narrow for the subject.

Affirmative limits are located: the E006 warning that threat tags may contain adjacent speakers, the absence of a printed final impact, and the explicit refusal to let current Sensei's speech or Plana's later choices stand for his. Not D: limits of attribution in one encounter, not a recurring pattern.
Bounded to the main-story Final volume (最終編) chapters 3-4 as maintained; no date, age or global ordering is supplied, and processing order is not dated chronology.

scenario_readiness.note: No located wording and uncertain tag ownership; any generated line would be invention. This bounds the evidence set, not the character.
One confrontation, one reported gift and one qualified inward request cannot support placing him in a new situation without inventing intention, voice and history.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: The Final-volume chapter 3-4 encounter and its reported aftermath as the monograph reads them; nothing before or after.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Shiroko (the alternate Shiroko of the encounter), current Sensei as counterpart, and the OS; the refusal applies equally to any other counterpart.
setting_constraints: Crossover, counterfactual or materially novel contexts are not supported.
No identification with current Sensei and no borrowing of his speech or motives.
No use of the uncurated checkpoints and episode readings the monograph cites.

scenario_readiness.note: The monograph explicitly records no ordinary-life basis: no hobby, meal, taste or routine.
A qualified care candidate is the only normative content, and the monograph refuses to supply his complete wishes or plan.
He is recognized as another Sensei, but the monograph supplies no school or club history, settled rank or evidence that the surrounding operations express his will.

known_limits.statement: Some Prenapates-tagged threatening lines may belong to adjacent speakers (E006); only the card gesture is securely represented as his act.

The gift of his escape resource to Shiroko is an OS report across an omitted interval; giver and recipient are contextually plausible, the transfer and its cost are not shown, and the OS interpretation of trust is hers.
No final impact, death, survival or controller or body diagnosis is supplied; current Sensei's reported return does not certify his fate.
Counterpart recognition does not establish numerical identity, shared memories or the same motives; current Sensei's explicit speech remains his own.
There is no evidence of ordinary life, tastes or routine for this subject.

The monograph is synthesized from maintained checkpoints and readings that are not curated on this subject; it claims no new primary, native or performed-voice reading, and the evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
